# `Q-26-6` — Inline lmd cell did not produce inlines

> An inline lmd cell evaluated to a value that is not an Inline, a list of Inlines, a string, a number, a boolean, or nil. The code span is left displayed and produces no output.

## What this means

An inline lmd cell, `` `{lmd} expr` `` in a paragraph, heading or list
item, replaces itself with the value of its expression, and that value has
to fit inside a line of text: an Inline, a list of Inlines (a
`pandoc.Inlines` or a plain table), a string, a number or a boolean
(written as `tostring` prints them), or `nil`, which makes the span
vanish. The expression evaluated to something else. The message names
what it was. The span stays displayed as code and produces no output.

## Why this happens

- The expression is a block fragment, `{=: … :=}`, or a `pandoc.Para`,
  `pandoc.Div` or other Block.
- The expression is a function or a table that is not a list of inlines.

## How to fix

Produce inlines. A block fragment becomes the inline form:

````markdown
Written `{lmd} {=[ *in italics* ]=}`.
````

A number needs nothing here: `` `{lmd} meta.version` `` with
`version: 12.1` in the front matter reads as `12.1`, and so does
`pandoc.Strong(meta.version)`. Wherever an Inline is expected, a number
or boolean reads as `tostring` would print it.

If the value really is a block, move it out of the paragraph into a block
cell.

- [`Q-26-5`](Q-26-5.qmd): the mirror image, for block cells.
- [`Q-26-3`](Q-26-3.qmd): an inline *fragment* that parsed to more than
